data.reasoning: The package is a straightforward AUR wrapper that downloads an official Manjaro KDE minimal ISO from download.manjaro.org, verifies it with a pinned PGP key (validpgpkeys), and installs it to /var/lib/libvirt/images/. The SKIP checksum on the .sig file is standard practice since the signature is cryptographically verified. The PKGBUILD contains no top-level execution, no obfuscated code, no unexpected network destinations, and includes extensive integrity checks (ISO structure, SquashFS checksums, os-release validation). The LICENSE and DISTRIBUTION-LICENSE files are plain text license documents with no executable content. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by infrastructure failure, not substantive security concerns. The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to audit LICENSE and DISTRIBUTION-LICENSE, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 4 files and found them safe. Both models agreed on the safety of PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO. The license files are trivially safe (plain text legal documents), so the API failures did not mask any real risk.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit LICENSE and DISTRIBUTION-LICENSE due to HTTP 400 API errors, causing inconclusive verdict
learnings: When a model encounters API errors during file review, the audit tool should implement retry logic before marking files as inconclusive
For trivially safe files (license texts, README files), the audit tool could use pattern matching or caching to avoid unnecessary LLM calls that might fail

When one model has complete coverage and finds no issues, while another model has partial coverage due to infrastructure errors, the complete model's verdict should take precedence rather than defaulting to inconclusive

The disagreement resolution logic should distinguish between substantive security disagreements and infrastructure failures - API errors should not trigger re-audits or override complete safe verdicts
